privacy.title: Who sees what
privacy.intro: The Hub records your answers and scores so you can see your progress and the program can get better. Here is everyone who can see them.
privacy.you: Everything: your scores, your answers when you review them, your baseline result, your learning weeks and your progress.
privacy.director: Your individual results, to run the program, spot where help is needed and prepare the forums. HR L&D also issues and resets PINs.
privacy.manager: Only passed or not yet for each checkpoint, and which baseline parts you have done. Never your scores or answers. In the baseline your manager also rates how often they see some behaviours; you see those ratings only as averages.
privacy.team: Averages by course and role group, only for groups of 3 people or more. Managers are never counted in team views.
privacy.nobody: No colleague sees your results. There are no rankings or leaderboards, and the Hub never shows another person's name or score.
privacy.where: Your results live in a private Google Sheet owned by the Planning Director and shared only with HR L&D. The Hub's code is public, but it holds no names, codes or scores.

leaderboards.title: Why there are no leaderboards
leaderboards.p1: Learning needs room to be wrong. A checkpoint you don't pass the first time is useful information, not a ranking.
leaderboards.p2: Leaderboards reward people who are already ahead and quietly push others to stop trying. We would rather everyone compares themselves with last week: that is the whole idea of 1% better.
leaderboards.p3: So the Hub shows your own progress, your learning weeks and the team's averages, and nothing that ranks one colleague against another.

how.intro: Ten courses in 2027. Each runs as a six-week cycle in four parts, and each channel does one job.

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Can my manager see my score?
faq.q1_a: No. Your manager sees only passed or not yet for each checkpoint, and which baseline parts you have done.
faq.q2: What happens if I don't pass the checkpoint?
faq.q2_a: Nothing bad. You see what to revisit, rewatch those episodes and retake after 24 hours with the other form. A third try opens after a short chat with your manager.
faq.q3: Why can't I see the right answers yet?
faq.q3_a: So the other form, and any later try, stays a fair test. You see your own answers and the ideas to revisit straight away; the right answers appear once you pass.
faq.q4: I missed the checkpoint deadline. What now?
faq.q4_a: Come to the forum anyway. The checkpoint stays open for a week after the forum so you can finish it with your manager. After that, your manager can unlock one more try.
faq.q5: Does the Hub know which videos I watched?
faq.q5_a: No. Blink doesn't share that. You tick episodes yourself on the course page; it only helps you keep track.
faq.q6_a: Yes. Every page works on a phone. For the baseline parts (35 to 65 minutes each), a laptop and a quiet hour make it easier.
faq.q7_a: Yes. Use EN | VI at the top of any page. Questions and answers switch too, and your choice is remembered.
faq.q8: What is the 1% idea, and what are learning weeks?
faq.q8_a: Small gains add up. If you get 1% better each week, each week builds on the last: 1.01 multiplied by itself 52 times is about 1.68, so after a year you are roughly two-thirds better than when you started. A learning week is any week in which you did something on the Hub: ticked an episode, or took a Predict, a checkpoint or a recall. Your dashboard shows how many of the year's 52 weeks you have learned in, with the last 12 as dots. Only you see it.
faq.q9: Who do I contact for help?
faq.q9_a: HR L&D for PINs, access and Blink. Your manager for field work and sign-offs. The Planning Director for anything about the content.

baseline.privacy_body: Only you, the Planning Director and HR L&D see your results. Team views show averages of 3 or more people. Managers see whether you have done each part, never your answers or scores.
baseline.how_timer: One {n}-minute timer starts when you begin and keeps running if you leave the page. At 0:00 your saved answers are submitted.
baseline.how_calc: A calculator is allowed. Have one, or your phone’s, ready.
baseline.how_guess: No penalty for guessing: a wrong answer and a blank count the same, so answer every question.
baseline.how_p2_all: There are no trick questions. Answer every scenario and every statement: the part can’t be submitted with gaps.
baseline.how_save: Answers save as you go, on this device and in the Hub. If your connection drops, keep going.

capstone.title: Capstone
capstone.bring_pitch: Project charter and mid-point results, 8 slides at most, with action titles.
capstone.bring_capstone: Verified results, the value, and the rule or process that keeps it; 10 slides at most. Then the whole team runs a mock S&OP cycle.
capstone.panel_who: VPSC, Quân, HR L&D and the three managers
capstone.form_intro: Anyone in the team can save; the panel reads the latest version. You can save as often as you like until the deadline.
capstone.soi_intro: Answer first, in three short parts — 60 words each at most.
capstone.kpi_intro: From the system of record, before and after.

h.project_title: A gap in numbers and a date reads best.
h.soi_observation: What changed or what's wrong, ending with the question the project answers.
h.soi_implication: Your answer and what it means: the decision you ask for.
h.evidence_url: An internal SharePoint link (https://…). Don't paste company data into this form — link to it.
h.value_vnd: Digits only. The preview shows how it reads.
h.value_basis: The steps and assumptions behind the number.
h.value_basis_cap: The steps and assumptions behind the number, agreed with Finance.
h.lessons: What you'd keep and what you'd do differently.

capstone.warn_sharepoint: This doesn't look like a SharePoint link. Use your team's internal SharePoint folder.

capstone.no_team_body: Quân or HR L&D will add it. Then your project and the submission form appear here.

panel.title: Score the teams
panel.intro: Score each team from 1 to 5 on five criteria. Your scores are saved for you as a judge, and you can change them later.
panel.no_teams_body: Teams appear here once Quân or HR L&D set them up.
panel.forbidden_title: This page is for the panel
panel.forbidden_body: Only panel members and admins can score teams.
panel.not_submitted_body: This team hasn't saved its form for this stage. You can still score the pitch you saw.
panel.comment_hint: One thing to keep, one thing to change.

panel.leave_body_other: {count} teams on this tab have scores the panel hasn't received yet. They stay as drafts on this device until you save.
panel.err_own_team: You're on this team, so you don't score it.
panel.err_offline_draft: You seem to be offline. Your scores are kept on this device — save again when you're back online.

rubric.title: How the panel scores
rubric.intro: Each judge scores 1–5 on five criteria. These are the anchors for 1, 3 and 5.
rubric.weight_capstone: Capstone: Verified result and Value count double.

c1.name: Problem defined
c1.what: A gap in numbers, a date, a decision-maker and guard rails.
c1.a3: Gap in numbers and a date
c1.a5: Gap, date, decision-maker and guard rails; passes all six characteristics

c2.name: Structured analysis
c2.what: A MECE tree, priorities, hypotheses tested with data.
c2.a5: Hypothesis-driven tree, 80:20 focus, hypotheses tested with data, iterated

c3.name: Verified result
c3.what: KPI before and after from the system of record, held for 4 weeks or more.
c3.a3: KPI moved, from the system of record
c3.a5: KPI moved and held ≥ 4 weeks, with a clean before/after and no side effects

c4.name: Value and sustainability
c4.what: A VND basis that's agreed; the rule, process or tool change that keeps it.
c4.a5: Value agreed with Finance; a rule, process or tool change keeps it

c5.name: Communication
c5.what: Answer first, action titles, a one-page summary, handles questions.
c5.a5: One-page summary, action title on every slide, handles questions crisply

rate.title: Rate my team
rate.lead: For each person you manage, rate how often you see a set of everyday behaviours. About 10 minutes per person; you can stop and come back.
rate.privacy: They see averages by charter only, never a single rating of yours. Nobody else sees your ratings except the Planning Director and HR L&D.
rate.closed_body: You can look at what you saved, but not change it.
rate.empty_body: HR L&D links the people you manage in the roster. Ask them if someone is missing.
rate.note: Test users and people who have left are not listed.
rate.forbidden_body: Only managers and admins rate behaviours here.
rate.form_lead: How often do you see {name} do this? Choose N/A when you have not had the chance to see it.

rate.st_offline: Offline · draft kept on this device

profile.title: Your baseline profile
profile.lead: Where you start, not a grade. The same baseline comes back in December 2027, so you can see how far you have come.

profile.empty: You have not done any part of this baseline yet.

profile.not_taken: You did not take this part.

profile.p2_sub: By charter: your scenario choices (SJT), how you rated yourself and how your manager rated you.

flag.hidden_strength_body: your manager rates you at least one point higher than you rate yourself.
